name.en: Fake An Post text asking you to pay a customs charge

how.en: Since 1 July 2026, parcels from outside the EU worth under €150 carry a €3 customs charge per item, and scammers use this. A text that looks like it is from An Post, a delivery company or Revenue says a parcel is held until you pay a small customs or delivery fee through a link. The page steals your card details. An Post never sends a payment link by text, and customs charges are never paid by consumers directly to Revenue.

text.en: A text from “An Post” or a courier says your parcel is held at customs.
It asks for a small customs or delivery fee.
You must pay through a link in the text.
It warns the parcel will be returned if you don’t pay soon.
AnPost: Your item from outside the EU is held at the Athlone hub pending a customs charge of €3.00 + VAT. Settle within 48 hours to release your delivery: [link]

en: an post text about customs charge
pay customs fee for my parcel
parcel held until i pay a small fee
text with a link to pay customs
delivery fee text with a link
A link in a text asking you to pay customs: An Post never sends payment links by text.
Any request for payment that claims to be from Revenue.
A small fee that asks for your full card details.
Don’t click. Check your parcel on An Post’s official website or app, typed in yourself.
If you paid through the link, call your bank straight away: your card details are now with the scammers.
Report it to the Gardaí. The CCPC can advise on customs charges.
